title: Genesis Gate Config
description: Project-level `.genesis/config.yaml` — the 'how' (provider selection, thresholds, BYO tooling) that complements the sealed Delivery Manifest (the 'what'). All optional; absent file means every gate auto-picks its default provider.

gates.description: Per-gate overrides keyed by gate name (e.g. secret-scan, dependency-scan).

provider.description: Provider key: a built-in scanner (e.g. trivy, gitleaks, semgrep, syft, pip-audit, pytest, llm, rules) or a generic BYO provider (command | report | external).

fail_on_severity.description: Findings at or above this severity fail the gate (overrides the provider's default pass/fail).

skip_dirs.description: Repo-relative directories the scanner must not look at — vendored dependencies, generated output, packaged sample/fixture apps that are scanned in their own right. Anchored at the repo root: "vendor" skips <repo>/vendor, not <repo>/packages/x/vendor (list nested trees explicitly). Honoured by the trivy (--skip-dirs) and semgrep (--exclude) providers; providers whose scanner has its own repo-level allowlist file (gitleaks → .gitleaks.toml) ignore it. A skipped directory is invisible to the gate, so give every entry a comment a reviewer can audit and keep your own source, infra and CI in scope.

command.description: For provider: command — the tool to run.

report.description: For provider: report — path to a scan result your CI already produced.

parser.description: How to normalize command output / an imported report into findings.

fail_on_nonzero.description: For provider: command — treat a non-zero exit as a failing gate.

attested_by.description: For provider: external — the system that handles this gate.

status.description: For provider: external — the recorded status (default passed, audit-noted).
